predecessors.name: Early Cholas
predecessors.text: the Chola country of the Kaveri delta: Kalabhras 'defeated the Cholas, Pandyas, and Cheras and established their rule'

predecessors.name: Early Pandyas
predecessors.text: the Pandya country around Madurai, taken by the Kalabhras (page undated)

predecessors.name: Early Cheras
predecessors.text: the Chera country, named with the Cholas and Pandyas as defeated by the Kalabhras (page undated)

successors.text: the north of the Tamil country: Simhavishnu 'consolidated his kingdom from south of the Krishna river and up to the Kaveri river by c.

ledger.x: 353: the Kalabhras hold the Tamil country.

c. 575: the Pallavas take the northern Tamil country. 'Simhavishnu consolidated his kingdom from south of the Krishna river and up to the Kaveri river by c. 575 CE.' The matching gain is in the Late Pallava dossier; Cliopatria draws it in 602 and keeps the Kalabhra shape whole until 591.

c. 590: the Pandya kingdom is revived at Madurai. 'The Pandya kingdom was revived by king Kadungon c. 560-590 CE'; Karashima 'dated Kadunkon's reign to 560 - 590 CE'. The page gives no separate date for the expulsion, so the year 592 is Cliopatria's.

wars.name: Pallava and Pandya overthrow of the Kalabhras
wars.outcome: The Kalabhras were removed; the Tamil country was divided between the Pallavas of Kanchi and the Pandyas of Madurai.

certainty.note: No page gives a border for the Kalabhras: the page itself calls them 'rulers of all or parts of Tamil region'; the whole life is an approximate extent.
